title: Staged ingress shaper and autoscale recovery playbook after GPU depletion
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-10 hosted-api experienced a multi-hour degradation where GPU pools servicing PROD region us-west-2 reached depletion. Symptoms were large request queues, excessive inference latency, and progressive denial of admission for non-priority tenants. This ticket captures the post-incident technical follow-ups: short-term mitigation (ingress shaping + emergency warm pools), autoscaler tuning, telemetry gaps, and longer-term architectural hardening (tenant scoring, cache isolation).

Technical root cause: A recent client-side multiplexing change increased short-burst, high-concurrency requests per-connection which amplified per-pool queueing; simultaneously the KV-cache rehydration pattern and a bad model-variant cache TTL led to cache pollution and increased warmup cost per request. The autoscaler had a conservative cooldown and a scale-up hysteresis tuned for steady traffic, which caused a 5–7 minute lag to reach required GPU capacity. Finally, our admission logic did not distinguish short inference fast-paths from long tail requests, so queue amplification favored long-running batches and starved fast requests.

Impact: Several high-traffic customers observed timeouts and elevated P99 latency; internal dashboards showed 4x increase in queued requests and a 20% drop in throughput for priority tenants during the event.

Scope of work in this ticket: 1) implement a staged ingress shaper that classifies and probabilistically admits short/long requests to reduce queue amplification; 2) lower autoscaler scale-up cooldown and add an opportunistic prewarm trigger based on tenant forecasting; 3) deploy a temporary emergency warm-pools feature that can be triggered by oncall to reduce warmup latency; 4) isolate model KV cache per-tenant for high-risk models and fix cache TTL regression; 5) improve telemetry (add burst-fingerprints, warmup-time histograms, per-tenant queue-depth timeseries); 6) update runbooks to include the new recovery playbook and ownership.

Decision notes and trade-offs: We evaluated changing the autoscaler to be more aggressive versus adding ingress shaping. Aggressive autoscaling reduces cold-latency but increases cost fast; ingress shaping reduces tail amplification at near-zero infra cost. We recommended a hybrid approach: short-term ingress shaping + modest autoscaler cooldown reduction + emergency warm-pools to balance cost and reliability. Permanent aggressive scale-up will be deferred until we have tenant forecasting with better signal.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged ingress shaper (canary on 10% of traffic in us-west-2), autoscaler cooldown config change first in canary, emergency warm-pools gated by RBAC for SREs, KV cache isolation behind config. Monitor warmup-time and queue-depth SLOs for 48 hours before expanding to 100%.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: Canary ingress shaper reduces queue amplification metric (queued_requests_peak) by >=40% vs baseline within 15 minutes of a synthetic burst
AC2: Autoscaler can increase available GPU pool count to target within <=180s during synthetic surge tests
AC3: Warmup-time p50/p95 for hot models drops by >=30% in canary region after emergency warm-pools enabled
AC4: No customer-facing errors introduced by canary rollout and SLOs are met for priority tenants during 48h observation
AC5: Telemetry dashboards for warmup-time and per-tenant queue-depth are live and linked in the runbook
comments: 2026-03-12: Initial triage completed. Incident attributed to combined ingress amplification and autoscaler hysteresis. Decided on hybrid mitigation approach.

2026-03-13: Drafted ingress shaper prototype. Benchmarked admission logic locally; initial synthetic bursts show 45% queue peak reduction without scale-up. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4891
2026-03-13: Telemetry gap identified — warmup latency not instrumented at tenant granularity. Data infra will add histograms and burst fingerprints. Ticketed as follow-up (DEP-thermo).
2026-03-14: Canaried autoscaler cooldown change in staging. Observed reduced time-to-capacity, no instability. Plan to promote to canary region after ingress shaper feature flag is in place.
2026-03-14: SRE playbook draft uploaded; emergency warm-pools flow added. Need oncall training session scheduled 2026-03-16.
